# Athreyas

Athreyas Yelishetti is a Site Reliability Engineer with fifteen years in
enterprise security and large-scale infrastructure. He is currently Senior
Staff SRE at Zscaler, working on zero-trust security platforms, and runs a
private home lab he writes about.

## About

- Full name Athreyas Yelishetti. Goes by Art.
- Senior Staff Site Reliability Engineer at Zscaler since December 2021.
- Fifteen years across SRE, infrastructure and enterprise security. Previously
  Akamai Technologies, Redcentric PLC and Citrix.
- Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA.
- Core skills: Python, Bash, Ansible, Terraform, AWS, Linux and FreeBSD,
  Kubernetes, Docker, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Nginx.
- Specialist areas: zero-trust and BeyondCorp architecture, SSO and RBAC,
  SAML and OAuth, identity management, observability and monitoring.
- Education: MBA (William Jessup University), MS Computer Science (Silicon
  Valley University), BTech Information Technology (JNTU Hyderabad).
- Runs a private home lab of self-hosted services behind a reverse proxy on a
  private network. Not publicly reachable, by design.
- Building toward customer-facing infrastructure architecture and forward
  deployment. Open to solutions architect and infrastructure-focused
  forward-deployed engineer roles, particularly at security, cloud and
  AI-infrastructure companies. MLOps and AI infrastructure are a study
  direction, not claimed production experience. Actively searching.
- Continuing education: completed Stanford Online XCS224N (Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning), 2026-09; XCS236 (Deep Generative Models) in progress since 2026-09-28.

## Projects

- [splitsheet](https://github.com/Athreyas/splitsheet) — Self-hosted
  Splitwise-style shared-expense tracker built on Google Sheets; settles debts
  in the fewest payments. Solves a real problem on infrastructure that already
  exists instead of standing up a new stack.
- [monk97.me](https://monk97.me) — This site. Hand-written static HTML with a
  keyboard-driven command prompt, no framework and no build step.
- [lab.monk97.me](https://lab.monk97.me) — live service health for the home lab, published as categories with no endpoints.

- All projects, with source links: https://monk97.me/projects/

## Writing

- [Publishing lab health without publishing the lab](https://monk97.me/work/lab-status)
  — case study: a public status page for a private network. Collector inside
  pushes to the Cloudflare edge; labels are an explicit allowlist; anything
  address-shaped is refused twice and fails closed. Written from public code.
- Index of case studies: https://monk97.me/work/
